_comment-vendored: VENDORED into vibe3d (task 0431). This is the `nfde` 0.1.3 D wrapper (Chance Snow, Zlib) plus a pinned copy of btzy/nativefiledialog-extended @ e092bbb under nativefiledialog-extended/. Two changes vs. the registry package: (1) the Linux backend is built with -DNFD_PORTAL=ON so file dialogs go through xdg-desktop-portal (out-of-process) instead of an in-process GTK3 chooser -- this drops the whole GTK/pango/gdk-pixbuf stack from the app; (2) the preBuildCommands no longer git-clone NFD at build time (the sources are vendored, so the build is hermetic and the NFD pin can never silently drift). source/nfde.d and nativefiledialog-extended/src/nfd_portal.cpp carry small local patches -- see third_party/nfde/PATCHES.md for the full patch list, upstream pins, and re-vendor procedure.
name: nfde
description: D bindings to Native File Dialog Extended (vendored, xdg-desktop-portal backend on Linux)
systemDependencies: CMake, Ninja, See `libs` and `lflags` for OS-specific dependencies.
_comment-prebuild: These commands must be INCREMENTAL. The linux/osx lines used to begin with `rm -rf $NFDE_PACKAGE_DIR/nativefiledialog-extended/out`, and it is tempting to call that harmless here because this package is a `staticLibrary`, so on a build where nothing changed dub finds its target up to date and never runs these commands at all -- unlike the vendored stb_image package that carried the identical line, which was a `sourceLibrary` with no artifact and therefore ran its commands on every single build (task 0662; it is now the d-stb-image shim). That is dormancy, not safety: the moment this package's OWN target goes stale (first build, `dub clean`, `--force`, any edit to source/nfde.d, a changed build id) the commands do run, and the wipe then discards the whole CMake tree and rebuilds the C++ backend from scratch -- measured on this host at 8.6s for that build against 6.4s once the wipe is gone, for a change that touched one line of D. Nothing was protected by it: every knob this build sets (-DNFD_PORTAL=ON, -DNFD_BUILD_TESTS=OFF, -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE) is passed as a `-D` on the `cmake -B` line, and a `-D` on the command line overwrites the value already in CMakeCache.txt and re-generates -- verified on this tree by flipping CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE over a warm build directory and watching both the cache entry and the recompile follow. Where a build directory genuinely cannot be reused (the package was moved, so the cached source path no longer matches) CMake refuses and says so, rather than quietly linking a stale library. So there is no rebuild-cleanliness need here to replace with an explicit clean target. The windows lines never had the wipe; all three platforms now agree.
